description:
About the Position

The Max Planck School of Biomedical AI (BMAI) offers a three-year interdisciplinary PhD programme at the interface of artificial intelligence and the life sciences. The programme brings together leading researchers from universities and research institutions across Germany and provides doctoral researchers with an international and highly interdisciplinary research environment. 25 fully funded PhD positions are available for the first BMAI cohort starting September 2027.

Research Areas

BMAI develops computational and AI methods across four interconnected research areas:

  • Understanding Molecular and Cellular Systems
  • Protein and Molecule Design
  • Learning Complex Biological Traits from Multi-Scale Data
  • Neural Network Exploration

Funding & Benefits

  • Fully funded PhD positions with competitive employment contracts at participating universities and research institutions.
  • Supervision by two BMAI Fellows.
  • International network of leading universities and research institutions across Germany.
  • Recurring one-week Schools with advanced interdisciplinary courses, scientific exchange, and career development.
  • Access to state-of-the-art research environments across participating institutions.
  • Support for annual participation in an international scientific conference.
  • Structured mentoring and professional development.

Eligibility and Requirements

  • Highly motivated and academically excellent candidates who will hold a Master's degree (M.Sc. or equivalent) by September of the year following their application.
  • Applicants typically have a background in computer science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, physics, or related fields.
  • Candidates from the life sciences are also encouraged to apply if they have a strong computational background and significant programming experience.
  • Working language: English.

Required Documents

  • Motivation letter
  • CV
  • Certificates
  • Transcripts

Application Process

Applications for the first BMAI cohort are open from 1 September to 1 December 2026. The PhD programme starts in September 2027. Visit the BMAI website for additional information and apply online.

About Max Planck School of Biomedical AI (BMAI)

Max Planck School of Biomedical AI provides doctoral training at the intersection of artificial intelligence and the life sciences. Based across a German research network, it brings together expertise in computing, biology and related disciplines. Researchers develop computational methods to investigate molecular systems, biological traits, biomolecular design and neural networks.

Official website: https://biomedicalai.maxplanckschools.org/en

Application dates

MilestoneDate
Application Opens1 September 2026
Application Deadline1 December 2026
Programme Start1 September 2027
Duration3 years

Official Link

  • Application Process: https://biomedicalai.maxplanckschools.org/4056/application-process
  • BMAI Website: https://biomedicalai.maxplanckschools.org/en

Contact

  • Email: bmai@maxplanckschools.de

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be sent to the contacts above or raised through the channel given on the official announcement page.

Important Notes

  • 25 fully funded PhD positions available.
  • Three-year programme starting September 2027.
  • English is the working language.
  • Master's degree required by September following application.
  • Interdisciplinary research at the interface of AI and life sciences.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: 1 December 2026. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.

Open the official application page ↗

Application guides

  • How to Email a PhD Supervisor: 7 Templates and Practical Tips
  • How to Read a PhD Job Advert: Funding, Eligibility and Application Steps
  • Studying in Germany: Tuition Fees, Living Costs and Funding

English language requirements

German doctoral employment generally has no fixed IELTS or TOEFL threshold; your English is judged from the written application and the interview, and prior English-medium study is widely accepted as evidence.
